cases.rationale: Untrusted HTML passed to jQuery DOM manipulation methods can execute attacker-controlled script in the page context, matching the browser-content branch's XSS leaf.
MOVEit Transfer incorporates attacker-controlled data into SQL operations, permitting database access through the query-injection branch's SQL-specific leaf.
A malicious same-parent-domain page can make authenticated Argo CD API requests on the victim's behalf because request origin and intent are not adequately verified.

Attacker-controlled Exchange backend-routing cookie values coerce the front end into unintended authenticated backend requests, establishing both server-side request forgery and the distinct authentication bypass that lets an unauthenticated attacker act as the Exchange server.

Broken path normalization lets crafted URLs resolve outside configured directories. In deployments with CGI enabled and permissive filesystem access, the same flaw can route a request to a system shell whose request body is interpreted as attacker-supplied shell syntax, independently establishing command injection as well as path traversal.
Bash executes attacker-supplied trailing shell commands embedded in environment-variable function definitions, specifically changing shell command syntax.
An exposed PHPUnit endpoint directly evaluates attacker-supplied PHP source from the HTTP request body, matching direct general-purpose code injection.
The Struts REST plugin reconstructs attacker-controlled XML objects with XStream without adequate type restrictions, enabling unsafe deserialization behavior.
Crafted DNS responses trigger stack-based buffer overflows in glibc resolver functions, making BufferOverflow the most specific descendant of out-of-bounds write.
Malformed TLS heartbeat packets cause OpenSSL to read beyond the intended buffer and return adjacent process memory, directly establishing an out-of-bounds read.
Chrome identified the underlying FileReader memory-safety defect specifically as a use-after-free, the most specific applicable temporal-memory label.
Failure to enforce authorization lets an unauthenticated attacker reset Confluence and create an administrator account; no narrower object-reference or request-origin mechanism applies.
Rapidly resetting an unbounded sequence of HTTP/2 streams consumes server work and stream-processing resources, causing denial of service through generic resource exhaustion.
The deployed file-upload component accepts arbitrary unauthenticated uploads through its exposed workflow, directly matching unrestricted file upload rather than a path or archive weakness.
